prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
As of September 2026, a new travel mood is becoming easier to see in Japan. Many young people, especially men, say they want to travel at their own pace. But actual stays are still often brief. The interesting story is not a complete change from sightseeing to long holidays. It is the gap between what travelers want and how long they actually plan to stay.

A 2025 survey found that, among men aged 29 and under, solo travel and hobby-focused travel were among the top choices. Each was chosen by about one in four respondents. Another survey found that about 90% of Japanese Gen Z respondents wanted free time during an overseas tour. Among them, about 80% wanted at least half a day free.

The wish becomes even longer when people imagine having more time. In one survey, the largest group, about 24%, said they would like to travel for about one week if they could take a month off. Yet a separate autumn survey from the same research group found that planned domestic stays were short. The average was 1.8 nights, and the median was similarly short.

That gap matters. A government report says the country still needs to increase travel frequency and lengthen stays. So the evidence points in two directions at once. The desire for more personal time is clear. A full shift to long, slow holidays is not.

【Point One】
Slow travel does not always mean taking a week off. It can mean having control over the hours you do have. A two-night trip may still feel slow if a traveler gives half a day to one hobby or leaves room to explore without a fixed list. For tour planners and local businesses, the question is not only trip length. It is how much freedom and depth the plan allows.

【Point Two】
The change is not the same for everyone. Men under 29 show stronger interest in solo and hobby-focused travel. For women in the same age group, visiting famous tourist sites remains highly popular, at about 45%. Solo travel is also the top travel-partner category for men aged 18 to 29 in another survey. Sightseeing is not disappearing; different purposes can exist side by side.

point_one.reasoning: 短期滞在でも、趣味に時間を割いたり予定を詰めすぎなかったりすれば「スロー」になり得るという具体的な解釈を加えている。旅行業者や地域事業者に対して、滞在日数だけでなく自由度や体験の深さを設計すべきだという実務的示唆もある。

point_two.reasoning: 男性の傾向だけでなく、同年代の女性では有名観光地巡りが約45%と人気であることを示し、変化が一様ではないと具体化している。したがって、若者全体が観光をやめたと解釈するのではなく、性別や旅行目的ごとに需要を分けて考える必要がある。
